title: Repeated-round halting probability bound
statement: Let $M$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, Boolean input and work-tape symbols, and state set $\mathrm{St}$, and let $\mathrm{Ready}$ be a predicate on configurations for a fixed Boolean input $x$. Fix a round length $R\in\mathbb N$ and a rational $a\ge 0$. Suppose that from every ready configuration, every choice word of length $R$ leads either to a halted configuration or to another ready configuration; and suppose that from every ready configuration, the probability of halting after a uniformly chosen length-$R$ choice word is at most $a$. Then for every $j\in\mathbb N$ and every ready configuration $c$, the probability that the machine halts after a uniformly chosen choice word of length $Rj$ is at most $a^j$.
hypotheses_covered: Machine has $k$ work tapes and Boolean symbols
Every length-$R$ run from a ready configuration halts or ends ready
Halting probability in each round from any ready configuration is at most $a$
